**DigitalT3 – AI-Enabled Learning Management System (LMS)**

DigitalT3 is an AI software services and consulting firm. This Learning Management System (LMS) is a strategic internal platform designed to embed training, evaluation, and readiness scoring into DigitalT3’s delivery lifecycle. The platform leverages AI to enhance learning, automate evaluation, and provide actionable insights for talent development and project readiness. It is built to be secure, scalable, GDPR-ready, and cloud-native, aligning with modern enterprise requirements.

The application is an AI-enabled LMS which requires a persistent data store; given the container type and name, the most appropriate detection is a database platform using MongoDB. No specific application framework is provided in the input, and the container's role is clearly a database server rather than a web/backend framework.
requirements: minimal mongod configuration for headless container (bind to 0.0.0.0 disabled unless required, or use container networking)
data directory (/data/db) mounted or created with correct permissions
environment variables for basic auth (MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME, MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD) if authentication required for dev
mongo-tools (mongo shell or mongosh) for basic DB operations
startup script/CMD to launch mongod in foreground (no systemd) for container process management
basic healthcheck command (e.g., mongo --eval 'db.runCommand({ping:1})') for container orchestration
lightweight backups: optional mongodump available for dump/restore in dev
minimal network ports exposed (27017) and no production monitoring/replica set configuration
optional lightweight init script to create minimal schemas/collections and seed test data for development

steps.name: Environment setup - data dir, permissions, and credential storage
steps.description: Create /data/db with safe permissions, verify mongod is present, validate and persist optional MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME/PASSWORD into workspace config (only when non-empty). Determine invoking non-root user via SUDO_USER/LOGNAME/USER and chown workspace config accordingly (avoid making root-owned files when invoked as root). Only export credentials to /etc/profile.d if EXPOSE_CREDS_IN_PROFILE=1 and credentials validated (opt-in). Avoid changing /data/db ownership unless a non-root mongodb runtime user is intentionally present. This step prepares filesystem and secure credential handling for automated non-interactive runs.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/lms_dt3-307785-309186/LMSDatabase(MongoDB)"
# create data dir with safe perms
sudo mkdir -p /data/db && sudo chmod 0755 /data/db
# verify mongod exists
command -v mongod >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'ERROR: mongod not found on PATH' >&2; exit 2; }
# ensure workspace config dir exists and set owner to invoking non-root user if available
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/config"
# determine preferred non-root owner
INVOKER="${SUDO_USER:-${LOGNAME:-${USER:-}}}"
if [ -n "$INVOKER" ] && id -u "$INVOKER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo chown -R "$INVOKER":"$INVOKER" "$WORKSPACE/config"
fi
# Persist credentials only when both variables are non-empty
if [ -n "${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  # validate no newlines and reasonable length
  case "$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME" in *$'\n'*|"" ) echo 'ERROR: invalid MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME' >&2; exit 3; ;; esac
  case "$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD" in *$'\n'*|"" ) echo 'ERROR: invalid MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD' >&2; exit 4; ;; esac
  credfile="$WORKSPACE/config/.mongo_dev_creds"
  printf 'MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME=%s\nMONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD=%s\n' "$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME" "$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD" > "$credfile"
  chmod 0600 "$credfile"
  if [ -n "$INVOKER" ] && id -u "$INVOKER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sudo chown "$INVOKER":"$INVOKER" "$credfile"
  fi
fi
# Optional: write profile.d only when explicitly opted-in and creds file present
if [ "${EXPOSE_CREDS_IN_PROFILE:-0}" -eq 1 ] && [ -f "$WORKSPACE/config/.mongo_dev_creds" ]; then
  # load and validate before writing
  . "$WORKSPACE/config/.mongo_dev_creds"
  if [ -n "${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    sudo bash -c "cat >/etc/profile.d/mongo_dev_env.sh <<EOF
# Opt-in dev creds for interactive shells (INSECURE: opt-in only)
export MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME='${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME}'
export MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD='${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD}'
EOF"
    sudo chmod 0640 /etc/profile.d/mongo_dev_env.sh
  else
    echo 'ERROR: creds invalid, skipping /etc/profile.d write' >&2; exit 5
  fi
fi
# Attempt to detect package mongodb runtime user (may be 'mongodb' or 'mongod') and only chown /data/db when non-root and intentional
MONGO_USER="$(awk -F: '/^(mongodb|mongod):/{print $1; exit}' /etc/passwd || true)"
if [ -n "$MONGO_USER" ] && [ "$MONGO_USER" != "root" ] && id -u "$MONGO_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  current_owner=$(stat -c '%u' /data/db || echo '')
  mongo_uid=$(id -u "$MONGO_USER")
  if [ -n "$current_owner" ] && [ "$current_owner" != "$mongo_uid" ]; then
    sudo chown -R "$MONGO_USER":"$MONGO_USER" /data/db
  fi
fi

  mongo_uid="$(id -u "$MONGO_USER")"

steps.name: Scaffold workspace and create runtime scripts (safe mongod start, healthcheck, init/seed)
steps.description: Generate scripts in the workspace/scripts directory with WORKSPACE expanded at generation time. Create a minimal mongod.conf that binds 127.0.0.1 by default. Provide start_mongod.sh that execs mongod in foreground and, if MONGO_BIND_ALL=1, passes --bind_ip_all to mongod (avoids brittle YAML edits). Generate healthcheck.sh and init_seed.sh with correct mongosh/mongo auth flag ordering, idempotent admin creation using provided credentials if present, and robust readiness loops. All generated runtime scripts use absolute paths and correct quoting to support non-interactive automation.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/lms_dt3-307785-309186/LMSDatabase(MongoDB)"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/scripts" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
# write minimal mongod.conf (bind to localhost by default)
cat > "$WORKSPACE/scripts/mongod.conf" <<YAML
storage:
  dbPath: /data/db
  journal:
    enabled: true
systemLog:
  destination: file
  path: /data/db/mongod.log
  logAppend: true
net:
  bindIp: 127.0.0.1
  port: 27017
YAML
# start_mongod.sh - exec mongod in foreground; if MONGO_BIND_ALL=1 add --bind_ip_all
cat > "$WORKSPACE/scripts/start_mongod.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONF="$SCRIPT_DIR/mongod.conf"
PIDFILE="/tmp/mongod_dev.pid"
# record pid (this process) then exec to keep same PID for mongod
printf "%d" "$$" >"$PIDFILE"
# build extra args
EXTRA_ARGS=()
if [ "${MONGO_BIND_ALL:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  EXTRA_ARGS+=(--bind_ip_all)
fi
# ensure mongod does not fork (foreground). exec so PID stays consistent.
exec mongod --config "$CONF" "${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"
BASH
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/scripts/start_mongod.sh"
# healthcheck.sh - uses auth flags before --eval; prefers mongosh when present
cat > "$WORKSPACE/scripts/healthcheck.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CREDFILE="$WORKSPACE/config/.mongo_dev_creds"
AUTH_ARGS=()
if [ -f "$CREDFILE" ]; then
  . "$CREDFILE"
  if [ -n "${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    AUTH_ARGS=(--username "$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME" --password "$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD" --authenticationDatabase admin)
  fi
fi
if command -v mongosh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mongosh "${AUTH_ARGS[@]}" --quiet --eval 'db.runCommand({ping:1})' >/dev/null
else
  mongo "${AUTH_ARGS[@]}" --quiet --eval 'db.runCommand({ping:1})' >/dev/null
fi
BASH
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/scripts/healthcheck.sh"
# init_seed.sh - waits for readiness, creates admin user using provided creds if admin absent, seeds sample data idempotently
cat > "$WORKSPACE/scripts/init_seed.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/lms_dt3-307785-309186/LMSDatabase(MongoDB)"
CREDFILE="$WORKSPACE/config/.mongo_dev_creds"
DBNAME="lms_dev"
AUTH_ARGS=()
ADMIN_USER=""
ADMIN_PASS=""
if [ -f "$CREDFILE" ]; then
  . "$CREDFILE"
  ADMIN_USER="${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME:-}"
  ADMIN_PASS="${MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-}"
  if [ -n "$ADMIN_USER" ] && [ -n "$ADMIN_PASS" ]; then
    AUTH_ARGS=(--username "$ADMIN_USER" --password "$ADMIN_PASS" --authenticationDatabase admin)
  fi
fi
# wait for readiness
for i in {1..30}; do
  if "$WORKSPACE/scripts/healthcheck.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
  if [ $i -eq 30 ]; then echo 'ERROR: mongod not ready' >&2; exit 6; fi
done
# check for admin users using JS that returns count
check_cmd="const u=db.getSiblingDB('admin').system.users.count(); print(u);"
if command -v mongosh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  admin_count=$(mongosh --quiet --eval "$check_cmd" "${AUTH_ARGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true)
else
  admin_count=$(mongo --quiet --eval "$check_cmd" "${AUTH_ARGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
admin_count=${admin_count:-0}
# if zero, create admin using provided creds or fail if none
if [ "$admin_count" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -z "$ADMIN_USER" ] || [ -z "$ADMIN_PASS" ]; then
    echo 'ERROR: no admin user present and no credentials supplied to create one' >&2; exit 7
  fi
  create_js="db = db.getSiblingDB('admin'); db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PASS', roles:[{role:'root',db:'admin'}]});"
  if command -v mongosh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    mongosh --quiet --eval "$create_js" || true
  else
    mongo --quiet --eval "$create_js" || true
  fi
fi
# seed sample document idempotently
seed_js="const d=db.getSiblingDB('${DBNAME}').courses; d.updateOne({title:'Intro'},{\$setOnInsert:{title:'Intro',created:new Date()}},{upsert:true});"
if command -v mongosh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mongosh "${AUTH_ARGS[@]}" --quiet --eval "$seed_js" || true
else
  mongo "${AUTH_ARGS[@]}" --quiet --eval "$seed_js" || true
fi
BASH
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/scripts/init_seed.sh"
